scope: Atomic file-backed WAL reclamation during explicit Raft compaction. Automatic production snapshots, snapshot transfer and durable production recovery remain incomplete.
changes: Core compaction passes its exact hard-state and borrowed log sequence to the storage replacement protocol
Stream only the hard-state, snapshot and retained suffix into a 0600 sibling file; fsync, rename and fsync the parent directory
Preserve old WAL and core state on failures before rename; require recovery after post-rename failure
Reject unreadable checkpoint state and disable read-time evaluation during WAL recovery

previousImplementation.result: First checkpoint leaves 8,457,942 bytes in the WAL, exceeding the 256 KiB retained-file assertion

faultTests: Repeated checkpoint reclamation preserves exact hard-state and suffix across reopen, truncation and append
Pre-rename file fsync failure leaves old WAL bytes and core boundary intact and removes temporary files
Post-rename directory fsync failure closes storage, rejects further writes and recovers the replacement snapshot and tail
Unreadable state cannot replace a valid WAL
Recovery rejects read-time evaluation even when its caller allows it

remaining: Production application snapshot capture and restore at the exact applied boundary, including membership
Snapshot catch-up for disconnected voters, witnesses and learners
Automatic retained log compaction and bounded lifetime retention in a production cluster
Production voter/witness hard-state and log recovery under podster-ucm.2.1
limitations: The memory fixture invokes explicit compaction on a standalone Raft state machine, not on a running production cluster.
Fsync errors are injected at real file and directory synchronization boundaries; no power-cut test was performed.
The native binary builds, but this checkpoint does not include a new native workload or privileged dataplane test.
Full-suite baseline and intermittent Node bootstrap failures recorded previously remain open.
